To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the order of activation of accessible genomic regions is consistent with their evolutionary ages and that this pattern is observed after mid-embryogenesis.
the developmental timing of activation of putative regulatory elements is correlated with the phylogenetic history of their appearance.

the accessibility of chromatin regions in vertebrate genomes tends to become activated in an order that reflects their phylogenetic order and this tendency is most pronounced during the phylotypic period of embryogenesis.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the molecular mechanisms underlying developmental transitions in gene regulatory elements and their evolutionary history, as well as with how these transitions are reflected in the evolution of gene regulatory networks.
a molecular mechanism that explains the evolutionary history of vertebrate development.
a molecular-level understanding of the relationship between evolution and development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the developmental hourglass model and the phylogenetic hierarchy are not mutually exclusive but rather complement each other.
developmental stages in vertebrate evolution are not necessarily recapitulated in terms of gene regulatory elements.
developmental transitions of chromating accessibility in the vertebrate species examined here recapitulated the phylogenetic transitions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evolutionary history of gene regulatory regions in vertebrates recapitulates the developmental hourglass.
evolutionarily newer gene regulatory elements are more frequently activated at later stages during embryogenesis.
the developmental transitions of gene regulations are recapitulated in a phylogenetic order.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the evolution of gene regulatory mechanisms is not a linear, one-way process but is instead a complex, dynamic process.
the evolution of gene regulation is recapitulated during embryogenesis in vertebrates.
the evolution of regulatory elements is a continuous process, in which the activation order of regulatory elements is correlated with their evolutionary age.
